Exhibit 99.1

 

Ethan Allen Reports First Quarter Results

 

DANBURY, CT – November 9, 2026 – Ethan Allen Interiors Inc. (“Ethan Allen” or the “Company”) (NYSE: ETD), a leading interior design destination, today reported its results for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026.

 

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, consolidated net sales were $129.6 million compared with $147.0 million in the prior year period. Consolidated gross margin was 59.6%; operating and adjusted operating margins were 1.3% and 2.2%, respectively. Diluted and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $0.07 and $0.10, respectively. Lower sales and tariffs pressured margins, partly offset by operating efficiencies. Retail and Wholesale segment written orders were down 1.2% and 1.3%, respectively, year over year, primarily due to lower design center traffic, a soft housing market, global unrest and U.S. midterm election uncertainty. Despite these challenges, Retail written orders in the first quarter rose 13.2% sequentially when compared with the Company’s fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and this momentum carried into the month of October, which saw a 0.3% increase.

 

The Company ended the first quarter with $92.2 million in cash and cash equivalents and no outstanding debt. During the quarter, Ethan Allen paid $92.2 million in cash dividends, comprising special dividends totaling $3.25 per share and a regular quarterly dividend of $0.39 per share, and invested $3.4 million in capital expenditures.

 

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS*

 

 

●

Consolidated net sales of $129.6 million; prior year $147.0 million

 

–

Retail net sales of $114.4 million; prior year $128.6 million

 

–

Wholesale net sales of $79.0 million; prior year $87.0 million

 

●

Written orders

 

–

Retail segment written orders declined 1.2%

 

–

Wholesale segment written orders decreased 1.3%

 

●

Consolidated gross margin of 59.6%; prior year 61.4%; current year impacted by incremental tariffs, higher designer floor sample sales and lower manufacturing production partially offset by a change in the sales mix, reduced headcount and a higher average ticket price

 

●

Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses decreased 5.8% from last year reflecting lower variable expenses, cost controls, reduced headcount and lower marketing costs

 

●

Marketing spend totaled $4.7 million or 3.6% of consolidated net sales; prior year 3.5%; the Company anticipates higher marketing expenses during the remainder of fiscal 2027

 

●

Consolidated operating margin of 1.3%; adjusted consolidated operating margin of 2.2%, compared with 7.2% in the prior year; current year operating margin impacted by higher tariffs and fixed cost deleveraging from lower consolidated net sales

 

●

Diluted EPS of $0.07; adjusted diluted EPS of $0.10; adjusted prior year $0.43

 

●

Paid cash dividends of $92.2 million compared with $16.4 million in the prior year

 

●

Capital expenditures of $3.4 million, compared with $2.4 million a year earlier; the increase supported new retail design centers, additional manufacturing equipment and technology upgrades

 

* See reconciliation of GAAP to adjusted key financial measures in the back of this release; comparisons are to the first quarter of fiscal year 2026

OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS

 

 

●

Opened new Company-operated design centers in Aventura (FL) and Victoria Gardens (CA), showcasing Ethan Allen home furnishings and combining complimentary interior design services with technology

 

●

Ended the quarter with 172 Ethan Allen retail design centers in North America, including 142 Company-operated and 30 independently owned and operated

 

●

Additional new design centers planned for fiscal 2027 include locations in Burlington (VT), Huntersville (NC) and Naples (FL)

 

●

New tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 became effective on July 24, 2026, and range between 10% and 12.5%; these tariffs replaced the previously issued 10% global tariffs imposed under Section 122

 

●

The quarter ended with 2,988 associates; 6.3% less than a year ago

 

●

Ethan Allen’s upholstery operation in Silao, Mexico was awarded the Great Place to Work® certification for the ninth consecutive year

 

●

The Company recently held its annual convention at its headquarters and livestreamed the event worldwide under the theme of We’re Just Getting Started; the program reviewed initiatives in manufacturing, logistics, technology, marketing and retail, and celebrated interior designers both for achievement in written sales and design excellence

 

●

More recently, on November 4, 2026, the Company held its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders; based on the final vote count, stockholders elected the following five directors to serve on its Board of Directors until the 2027 annual meeting: Douglas G. Bergeron, Maria Eugenia Casar, Kristine E. Miller, Stephen Oblak and Tara I. Stacom

 

BALANCE SHEET and CASH FLOW

 

 

●

Cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $92.2 million at September 30, 2026 compared with $187.5 million at June 30, 2026; decrease of $95.3 million reflects the payment of $92.2 million in cash dividends and capital expenditures of $3.4 million

 

●

Cash used in operating activities totaled $0.8 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, a decrease from $16.8 million provided by operating activities in the prior year due to lower net income, incremental restructuring payments and working capital changes partially offset by insurance proceeds received

 

●

Cash dividends paid totaled $92.2 million, including special dividends of $3.25 per share in addition to a regular quarterly dividend of $0.39 per share

 

●

Net merchandise inventory levels totaled $153.8 million at September 30, 2026, up 3.6% since June 30, 2026, reflecting new product introductions and price increases

 

●

Customer deposits from undelivered written orders totaled $74.3 million at September 30, 2026, up from $62.7 million at June 30, 2026 as the pace of incoming Retail segment written orders improved and outpaced delivered sales

 

●

Wholesale backlog was $55.0 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.7% over the prior year

 

●

No outstanding debt at September 30, 2026, and credit availability of $121.5 million

DIVIDENDS

 

On July 28, 2026, the Board of Directors declared a $0.25 per share special cash dividend in addition to a $0.39 per share regular quarterly cash dividend, both payable on August 26, 2026 to shareholders of record as of August 12, 2026. In addition, on August 19, 2026 the Board declared a special $3.00 per share dividend to shareholders of record as of September 3, 2026, payable September 17, 2026.

 

ABOUT ETHAN ALLEN

 

Ethan Allen (NYSE:ETD) is a leading interior design destination combining state-of-the-art technology with personal service. Ethan Allen design centers, which represent a mix of Company-operated and independent licensee locations, offer complimentary interior design service and sell a full range of home furnishings, including custom furniture and artisan-crafted accents for every room in the home. Vertically integrated from product design through logistics, the Company manufactures about 75% of its custom-crafted furniture in its own North American manufacturing facilities and has been recognized for product quality and craftsmanship since 1932. Learn more at www.ethanallen.com and follow Ethan Allen on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn. 

 

Investor Relations Contact:
IR@ethanallen.com

 

ABOUT NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES

 

This release is intended to supplement, rather than to supersede, the Company's consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). In this release the Company has included financial measures that are derived from the consolidated financial statements but are not presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company uses non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted operating income and margin, adjusted net income and adjusted diluted EPS (collectively “non-GAAP financial measures”). The Company computes these non-GAAP financial measures by adjusting the comparable GAAP measure to remove the impact of certain charges and gains and the related tax effect of these adjustments. Investors should consider these non-GAAP financial measures in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial performance measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. The Company uses these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision making and to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. The Company believes that they provide useful information about operating results, enhance the overall understanding of past financial performance and prospects, and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision making. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable financial measure reported in accordance with GAAP is provided at the end of this release.

Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

 

To supplement the financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP, the Company uses non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted operating income and margin, adjusted net income and adjusted diluted EPS. The reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP are shown in tables below.

 

These non-GAAP measures are derived from the consolidated financial statements but are not presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company believes these non-GAAP measures provide a meaningful comparison of its results to others in its industry and prior year results. Investors should consider these non-GAAP financial measures in addition to, and not as a substitute for, its financial performance measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. Moreover, these non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in that they do not reflect all the items associated with the operations of the business as determined in accordance with GAAP. Other companies may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures differently than the Company does, limiting the usefulness of those measures for comparative purposes. Despite the limitations of these non-GAAP financial measures, the Company believes these adjusted financial measures and the information they provide are useful in viewing its performance using the same tools that management uses to assess progress in achieving its goals. Adjusted measures may also facilitate comparisons to historical performance.
